leads.name: The Peter-Linde

location.address: Burgwall, Burg Coppenbrügge, 31863 Coppenbrügge, Niedersachsen, Germany

leads.access: Free. Stands on the castle wall (Burgwall) reached by a public footpath right before the castle gate; the castle grounds and wall walk are open to the public outside museum hours (museum open Thu-Sun and holidays 14:00-17:00, castle park otherwise walkable).
leads.transport: In the town centre of Coppenbrügge; free parking at the castle, reachable by regional bus.
leads.verify_notes: Single-tree-destination candidate (2026-08-31 exception): a summer linden (Tilia platyphyllos) growing directly on the stone castle wall of Burg Coppenbrügge, its short trunk partly rooted into and over the masonry. Two independent sources agree: baumkunde.de (last field observation 13 Feb 2022, girth 6.6m at 50cm height, height 11.0m, vital with a masonry-filled hollow and crown-securing cables) and de.wikipedia's Burg Coppenbrügge article (girth 6.64m as of 2017, same age range, designated Naturdenkmal). Named for a 1697 visit by Tsar Peter I of Russia, part of a diplomatic meeting with Electress Sophie of Hanover known as the 'Damenfrieden von Coppenbrügge' (Ladies' Peace of Coppenbrügge), said to have helped avert war between Austria and Brandenburg-Prussia. Depicted in a Merian engraving from 1654 (predating the Peter connection, so the tree itself is confirmed older than the 1697 legend). An 18th-century (1718) source describes it having been trained for roughly a century as a three-storey walkable tree bower entered directly from the castle's first floor; today the crown is irregular with most of the old trained branches broken away. Age given as a range (500-700y) by both sources, not narrowed further. Girth recorded as both 660cm (baumkunde, 2020 measurement) and 664cm (Wikipedia, 2017 measurement); used baumkunde's more recent figure, both close enough to be the same growth. No conflicting facts beyond the ordinary growth between measurements. Anecdote to lead with: a linden that people once climbed INTO, via a room built inside its living branches, to drink with a future Tsar.
